core_obligations: Set up the diagram (proof lines 5236-5245): the 2-morphism is a transformation of the pullback functors whose composition with the structure sheaf map is unchanged, displayed as a commutative triangle.

Test on affine etale objects (proof lines 5246-5287): for an affine etale V over the target, an immersion of V into affine n-space over the target gives injections of representable sheaves, whose base change gives injections after pulling back; with the identification of pullbacks of representable sheaves one obtains a square whose right side commutes by hypothesis and whose horizontal composites are injective, so the left vertical arrow is the identity.

Propagate to all sheaves (proof lines 5288-5294): every sheaf of sets on the small etale site receives a surjection from a coproduct of representable sheaves with affine representing objects, so the transformation is the identity everywhere.
proof_roadmap: Translate the 2-morphism into a compatible transformation of pullback functors.
Test it on representable sheaves attached to affine etale schemes using injections into a product of copies of the structure sheaf.
Conclude on all sheaves by the generation of the topos by such representables.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the rigidity statement that the identity is the only 2-morphism of the locally ringed topos attached to a morphism of schemes, that is, the pullback functor is rigid (statement lines 5226-5233). The proof is a complete argument: the compatibility with the structure sheaf maps is displayed (proof lines 5236-5245); the transformation is tested on the representable sheaves attached to affine etale schemes by embedding them into affine space and using the resulting injections of sheaves and the identification of pullbacks of representables, so that injectivity of the horizontal composites forces the transformation to be the identity on those generators (proof lines 5246-5287); and generation of the topos by such representables extends the conclusion to all sheaves (proof lines 5288-5294). The non-formal content is the reduction to generators and the injection test. The claim is H2: a structured argument with every input named.
